question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution:
The correct answer is **"whom."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Whom" **is used as an object pronoun, while **"who"** is used as a subject pronoun.
 
• When referring to the object of a sentence or clause,** "whom"** is the correct choice.
 
• **Example:**
 
• *"To whom were you speaking?" *(correct)
 
• * "Who were you speaking to?*" (incorrect)
 
• So, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
• Correct passage*:*

Dill ate, and ate and ate. He hadn’t eaten since__ last night. He used all his money for a ticket, __boarded__ the train, as he had done many times, coolly chatted with the conductor, to __**whom**__ Dill was a familiar sight, but he had not the nerve to invoke the rule on small children travelling a distance alone; if you’ve lost your money the conductor will ______ (4) ______ you enough for dinner and your father will ______ (5) ______ him back at the end of the line. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **"Who"** is a subject pronoun and is not appropriate for referring to the object of a sentence or clause.
 
• **"Whose"** is a possessive pronoun and does not fit the grammatical structure of the sentence.
 
• **"Whoever"** is a pronoun used to refer to any person who (fill in the blank), but is not the correct choice for this sentence.
